title: Program timeline
intro: Selected milestones in the development of the program, from balloon mapping in 2017 to current field research.

milestones.title: Balloon mapping and field GIS
milestones.summary: Students from three Columbia GIS courses combined balloon aerial imagery with GPS and mobile field observations at Black Rock Forest.
milestones.details: Public Lab balloon kits carried visible and modified-infrared cameras. High winds limited the balloon operation; usable images and ground observations supported GIS instruction.

milestones.title: Equipment for drone and 3D GIS teaching
milestones.summary: Columbia's Emerging Technology Grant supported drone and visualization equipment for GIS teaching.
milestones.details: The grant supported Drones and AR/VR for 3D Modeling in GIS. Later course fieldwork used that equipment for aerial observation and spatial analysis.

milestones.title: Callicoon field exercise
milestones.summary: SDEV3450 students collected drone imagery and field observations during a two-day exercise and used the data to develop spatial analyses.
milestones.details: Kytt MacManus and teaching assistant Juan Nathaniel led the field exercise. Students developed spatial analyses and a joint StoryMap.

milestones.title: Staten Island community mapping
milestones.summary: SDEV4650 students and community partners collected drone imagery around 60 Hannah Street and developed a 3D reconstruction.
milestones.details: Collaboratory support included a teaching drone. Follow-up work helped the Staten Island Urban Center access student StoryMap content and map layers.

image.alt_text: Participants and a marked landing pad on the 60 Hannah Street rooftop.

milestones.title: William Paterson tree-mapping workshop
milestones.summary: Nicole Davi hosted a workshop connecting Field Maps tree observations with drone imagery and surface products.
milestones.details: Visible and thermal observations complemented tree records and later elevation products. These displays do not establish tree-identification performance.

image.alt_text: Workshop participants gathered on grass at William Paterson University.

milestones.title: NYC Parks drone research begins
milestones.summary: EFPL and Natan Charytan began permitted drone mapping and repeat observations at Four Sparrow Marsh.
milestones.details: Kytt MacManus identifies April 18 as the first UAS operation approved by NYC Parks. Wind curtailed that operation; the team returned on May 2. The photograph shows the return visit.

image.alt_text: Field collaborators standing beside the marsh during the Four Sparrow return survey.

milestones.title: North Shore and Morningside mapping
milestones.summary: Separate flights mapped North Shore Esplanade on December 1 and Morningside Park on December 18.
milestones.details: North Shore continued the Staten Island community collaboration. Morningside surface and terrain products support continuing research.

image.alt_text: Collaborators using a handheld drone controller during North Shore fieldwork.

milestones.title: Ground and aerial field methods
milestones.summary: SDEV3450 students and WAC partners combined positioning observations with photogrammetry, LiDAR and other field instruments.
milestones.details: The photogrammetric products and the logged IF1200A LiDAR acquisition are different measurement systems. Ground observations supported the field exercise.

image.alt_text: Paired camera views of the Hemlock field group and equipment on a grass field; no farm buildings are shown.

milestones.title: UNZA teaching and exchange
milestones.summary: University of Zambia and HOT colleagues shared field collection, photogrammetric processing and interpretation methods.
milestones.details: Working sessions and field collaboration used campus mapping as material for teaching and exchange. The working-session photograph is dated to June 2026.

image.alt_text: Collaborators seated around a meeting table during the UNZA technical exchange.

milestones.title: Mapping selected sites around Mtukuzi
milestones.summary: Local collaborators and UNZA colleagues documented selected village, school, agricultural, river and water-well sites.
milestones.details: The mapping covers selected sites, not the wider catchment. Fieldwork also supplied material for Raphael Sutiono and Kytt MacManus's TOPSTSCHOOL contribution.

image.alt_text: Orthomosaic of selected village and school-area buildings, paths, vegetation and cultivated land near Mtukuzi.

milestones.title: SAMARA participates in the DARPA Lift Challenge
milestones.summary: Team SAMARA participated in the DARPA Lift Challenge in Dayton as part of heavy-lift aircraft development connected to aerial logistics for electrification.
milestones.details: The team reached the spin-up testing stage. Aircraft development continues with a focus on remote payload delivery and utility operations.

image.alt_text: DARPA Lift Challenge event banner with a collage of competing aircraft.

milestones.title: Highbridge aerial mapping and 3D documentation
milestones.summary: Permitted DJI survey flights and a closer-range Skydio mission documented Highbridge Park and its water tower on November 16.
milestones.details: Initial processing produced orthomosaics, surface and terrain products, point clouds and a textured reconstruction of the tower area.

image.alt_text: The Highbridge water tower, pool and surrounding autumn tree canopy viewed from a drone.

milestones.title: Terrain and wind research
milestones.summary: EFPL researchers use terrain and surface geometry to investigate wind observations and airflow at Lamont.
milestones.details: DURIP supported IF1200A instrumentation for ARO research. Maps and reconstructions describe the site; they do not by themselves test a wind model.

image.alt_text: Oblique view of a sampled Lamont photogrammetric point cloud, with exaggerated vertical scale.
